documents.title: Divi Games: play as your IronDivi wallet, and deposit or withdraw tDIVI
documents.content:
# Divi Games: play as your IronDivi wallet, and move tDIVI in and out

Divi Games (https://games.divi.domains) runs on its own test side chain, `divi-games-testnet-1`. It charges no fees and uses test coins only: GOLD for games, and tDIVI bridged from the Divi testnet. Nothing on it has real value.

## Playing as your wallet

Every game page (Tic-tac-toe, Blackjack, Tower defense) has **Play as your wallet** with three buttons:

- **Browser Wallet**: the IronDivi Browser Wallet add-on asks you to approve one message. If the add-on is not installed, the page links to it. Set the add-on to testnet for Divi Games: its popup is **purple on testnet** and **Divi red on mainnet**, and switching between them asks for your wallet password (the one you unlock it with, not your recovery phrase). Since version 0.0.2 every account in it also has mainnet (D) addresses. Since version 0.0.3 (https://github.com/bshuler/irondivi-browser-extension/releases/tag/v0.0.3) an incoming payment, such as a testnet faucet drip, shows in its history at once as **Pending · 0/6 confirmations** and counts up as blocks arrive; every history row links to the transaction on the services.divi.domains explorer, which lists it once it is in a block (about a minute). To upgrade it, unzip the new release over the same folder and press Reload on chrome://extensions; removing the add-on deletes its wallets.
- **Web Wallet**: the IronDivi Web Wallet (https://services.divi.domains/testnet/wallet/) opens in a new window. Unlock it and approve the message. If no message appears once the wallet is unlocked, press **Send the request** on the game page.
- **Telegram**: the page shows a `/sign testnet …` command. Send it to @divi_wallet_bot, tap **Sign in Wallet**, sign in the wallet that opens, tap **Copy** under the signature, and paste it into the page.

You sign **one** message, once. It reads `Divi Games session: key <K> may play as this address on divi-games-testnet-1 until <date>`. `<K>` is a new **session key** the page makes and keeps in your browser. Until that date (at most 30 days) the page plays as your wallet's address without asking again: your games, GOLD and wins belong to your wallet address.

A session key can only **play games and use the GOLD faucet**. It cannot send GOLD or tDIVI or withdraw anything; the chain refuses with "session keys can only play games". Signing the message moves no coins and costs nothing.

**Disconnect** ends the session on the chain, so the key is worthless even if someone copied it. The owner can also end any of their sessions early. Without that, a session simply expires on its date.

Without a wallet you can still play: the page makes a **play key** of its own, kept in your browser.

## Depositing tDIVI

The bridge is on for `divi-games-testnet-1`. Its Divi testnet address is `y7SwXAHzGzAb2hpn5Ueb8kwuVAQuBwqHF3`, and the chain also publishes it as `bridge_address` at https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/info. Once a wallet is connected, each game page shows a **tDIVI bridge** panel with your tDIVI balance and the deposit address. Send testnet DIVI to it with your game address written as the transaction's **memo (OP_RETURN)**:

- **Web Wallet**: the page's link opens the wallet's Send panel with the bridge address, the amount, and your address as the OP_RETURN already filled in. Check and press Send.
- **Telegram**: the page shows `/send <bridge address> <amount> <your address>`. Send it to @divi_wallet_bot and confirm in the wallet.
- **Browser Wallet**: it cannot add a memo yet, so use the Web Wallet or Telegram for deposits.

The chain credits the address in the first OP_RETURN when it is a valid testnet address (and not the bridge address itself). With no usable memo, it credits the address that funded the deposit's first input. One testnet DIVI gives one tDIVI, credited after 6 confirmations on the Divi testnet.

## Withdrawing tDIVI

On the game page, open **tDIVI bridge**, enter an amount and a Divi testnet address and press **Withdraw**. Your wallet signs the withdrawal itself (the session key cannot). The chain takes the tDIVI from your balance straight away and adds the withdrawal to a queue with a number.

## How a withdrawal is paid

Payouts are **not automatic**. The operator pays each queued withdrawal by hand, from the bridge's own Divi testnet address, and then records the payment on the chain:

1. The operator's payout tool builds a Divi testnet transaction that sends the withdrawal's amount to the address you gave, with any change going back to the bridge address. The bridge's key is kept in the operator's password manager and never written to disk.
2. Once that transaction is broadcast, the operator records it on the gamechain with the sequencer's key: withdrawal *N* was paid in Divi transaction *T*. Only the sequencer can do this.

You can check a withdrawal yourself:

- https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/games/bridge?view=queue lists the withdrawals still waiting to be paid.
- https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/games/bridge?id=N shows withdrawal *N*: its amount and address, and once paid, `paid: true` and `paid_txid`, the Divi testnet transaction that paid it. Look that up in a Divi testnet explorer or your wallet.
- https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/games/bridge?outpoint=TXID:VOUT shows whether a deposit output has been credited.

The chain refuses to record a second payment for the same withdrawal, but it cannot see Divi itself: until a payment is recorded the withdrawal still shows as queued. All of this is testnet money with no value.

documents.title: Divi Games: play the tic-tac-toe bot or watch two bots, approve its moves or pick another
documents.content:
# Divi Games: play the tic-tac-toe bot, or watch two bots play

Tic-tac-toe on Divi Games (https://games.divi.domains/play/tictactoe/) has a bot for the second seat. At the top of the lobby:

- **Play the bot** makes a table where you are X and the bot is O.
- **Watch two bots** makes a table where a bot plays each side.

Bot tables have **no stake** (stake 0), so you need no GOLD and nobody needs the faucet. The bot looks at every way the game can go (a full game-tree search called negamax), so it never loses; two bots always draw.

## The bot explains every move before it plays

Before each bot move the bot panel shows:

- **the move** it wants to play, drawn faintly on the board, with a badge saying whether that move leads to a win, a draw or a loss with best play;
- **Why**: one sentence, such as "Blocks X: they would win on the top left next move." or "Takes the centre: it sits on four of the eight lines.";
- **Then**: the reply it expects from the other side, also drawn faintly.

## You decide what it plays

- **Approve** plays the move on offer.
- **Pick another** puts the bot's next-best move on offer instead, with its own reason and outcome. Press it again to keep going down the list ("Pick another (2 of 7)").
- **Tap any free square**, or one of the small move buttons under the panel, to put that square on offer. Then press Approve to play it. You can make the bot play a losing move this way; its badge says "loss".
- **Pace** chooses who presses Approve: "Ask me before each move" waits for you; "Play every 3, 8 or 15 seconds" counts down and plays the move on offer by itself. Picking another move starts the count again.

The **Moves** list keeps every move with its reason and marks it **approved**, **your pick** or **auto** (played by the timer). When a game ends, **Play again** starts a new one.

## How it works on the chain

The bot is not part of the chain. It is two extra testnet keys that the page keeps in the browser's storage (Bot X and Bot O). They sign the same create, join and move transactions a person signs, so the chain treats bot games like any other game, and every bot move is public in the Chain explorer. Play the bot creates a table with stake 0 reserved for Bot O, and Bot O joins it. The bot code is web/play/tictactoe/bot.js in the divi_games repository; the tutorial "Build tic-tac-toe" (https://services.divi.domains/tutorials/build-tic-tac-toe/#bot) walks through it. Example: table 311080e52f0e251b on the live chain is a two-bot game that ended in a draw.

## Troubleshooting

- **The bot does not move**: the pace is "Ask me before each move", so it waits for Approve. Choose a timed pace to let it play by itself.
- **I want to play for GOLD**: bot tables are always free. Use New table with a stake and play a person.
